page: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. The instance delivers 96 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 192 GB of memory, which establishes a standard compute-optimized ratio of 2 GB RAM per core. Cache sizing features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 96 MB of L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is supported via AES instructions, whereas x86-specific vector extensions and simultaneous multithreading are absent by design. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not present, and the instance does not feature local storage, relying entirely on remote EBS volumes over its 50 Gbps baseline network fabric.

Benchmark results highlight substantial parallel throughput driven by the 96 independent physical cores. Multi-core performance is categorized in the top tier across tests such as stress-ng multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which reached 1131.71 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 363.83 GB/sec, placing memory throughput in the top tier as well. While multi-threaded execution and extended instructions rank in the top percentiles, single-core CPU throughput remains within average boundaries, as seen in stress-ng single-core tests. In application benchmarks, the instance recorded 269.45 million Redis SET operations per second and 198.56 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs, meaning high I/O storage pipelines require network-attached storage allocation. However, the high core density and uniform non-hyperthreaded physical cores offer notable compute efficiency for scale-out workloads. The hardware profile is well suited for CPU-bound distributed workloads, including microservices fleets, batch video encoding, continuous integration build clusters, Redis in-memory caches, high-concurrency static web serving, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V3 architecture clocked at 3.3 GHz. Configured without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers one hardware thread per core alongside 192 GB of system memory, matching a 2 GB per core ratio. Cache layout consists of 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 96 MB L3 cache. The instance includes 50 Gbps baseline networking, no local disk storage, and no GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the platform demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing, memory bandwidth exceeding 363 GB/sec, and strong key-value throughput with 269.45 million Redis SET operations per second, contrasted by average single-thread performance. The instance fits CPU-bound scale-out tasks such as high-density web serving, distributed batch processing, CI/CD build pipelines, and lightweight model inference.
